comparison: Perfect agreement on ERQC component identification and characterization (C58-C81). Both evaluations find the sequence analysis, phylogenetic analysis, domain analysis, and homology comparisons well-supported with appropriate methodologies and controls.

Strong agreement on N-glycan profile alterations (C2, C82-C93). Both evaluations affirm the HPLC and MALDI-TOF data as convincing evidence with rigorous, well-controlled assays. Peer review also includes C94-C95 (mnl1Δ/mnl2Δ findings) which OpenEval addresses separately in R18.

Agreement on stress response and growth defects (C96-C106). Both find gene expression and spotting assay data support stress-responsive upregulation and Ugg1's role in stress tolerance. Peer review also includes ER stress markers (C109-C113) which OpenEval addresses in R4 and R5.

Both support ER stress findings (C109-C112). OpenEval finds TFL sensitivity and HXL1 splicing provide direct evidence for ER stress, though notes direct misfolded protein measurement would strengthen conclusions. Peer review groups this with broader stress response data.

Both support ER localization evidence (C113). OpenEval specifically highlights fluorescence microscopy colocalization data, while peer review includes this as part of comprehensive stress response characterization.

Perfect agreement on virulence factor defects (C3, C114-C118). Both evaluations find melanin production and capsule staining assays provide quantitative evidence for virulence factor impairment with appropriate documentation of differential severity between mutants.

Strong agreement on virulence attenuation (C5, C119-C126). Both find mouse survival studies, fungal burden assays, and macrophage survival assays provide comprehensive evidence with appropriate statistical analysis. Peer review also includes C4 which OpenEval does not separately address.

Agreement on capsule defect mechanisms (C6, C129-C141). Both support GXM blotting and capsule transfer data showing distinct mechanisms. OpenEval notes trafficking defect interpretation is well-supported but polymer size claims are more speculative. Peer review also includes broader secretion and structural findings (C7, C127-C128, C142-C151) addressed in OpenEval R9 and R12.

Both support cellular structural alterations (C142-C150). OpenEval finds TEM and staining data provide clear visual evidence, though notes functional significance requires further investigation. Peer review groups these observations with capsule and secretion defects as part of overall ERQC involvement.

Agreement on transcriptomic findings (C8, C152-C161). Both find RNA-seq data demonstrates significant differential gene expression with appropriate GO analysis. OpenEval notes ER stress response interpretation is well-supported; peer review accepts this as part of appropriate methodologies.

Both support post-transcriptional mechanism conclusion (C10, C162). OpenEval highlights qRT-PCR showing no transcriptional changes as important negative result. Peer review includes this within broader transcriptomic analysis acceptance.

Agreement on selective enzyme secretion defects (C7, C163-C169). Both find enzyme activity assays provide quantitative evidence. OpenEval notes urease secretion interpretation is reasonable but could be strengthened; peer review accepts differential secretion pathway effects as well-supported.

Both support conventional secretion findings (C170-C173). OpenEval finds Western blot data demonstrates unperturbed conventional secretion but notes reliance on single marker. Peer review accepts this as part of evidence distinguishing secretion pathway effects.

Strong agreement on EV biogenesis defects (C11, C174-C182). Both find NTA and cryo-TEM data provide comprehensive quantitative and visual evidence with appropriate statistical analysis. Peer review emphasizes this as key contribution with solid data.

Agreement on EV proteomic changes (C185-C190). Both support proteomic data showing substantial EV composition changes. OpenEval notes biological significance requires further investigation; peer review treats this as part of overall EV contribution.

Both support GXM cargo loading defect (C191-C192). OpenEval highlights Western blot showing GXM absence in EVs as strong evidence for cargo loading defects. Peer review includes this as part of comprehensive EV analysis demonstrating involvement in composition.

Agreement on overarching conclusions (C12-C14, C57, C196, C202, C204). Both find cumulative evidence supports ERQC's role in fitness and virulence factor secretion. OpenEval emphasizes pleiotropic effects; peer review affirms conclusions while noting mechanisms 'not yet fully understood.'

Both support mnl1Δ/mnl2Δ findings (C94-C95, C107-C108). OpenEval finds no significant phenotypes with reasonable speculation about ERAD substrates. Peer review includes these claims within broader N-glycan profiling acceptance.

Agreement on C. neoformans ERQC uniqueness (C193-C195). Both accept phylogenetic characterization of unique ERQC composition. OpenEval cites supporting data; peer review treats this as established context and novelty claim.

Both support contextualization with prior literature (C197-C201). OpenEval finds discussion appropriately contextualizes ER stress and thermotolerance findings. Peer review accepts these as part of well-supported overall conclusions about ERQC involvement.

Agreement on unconventional vs conventional secretion (C203, C205, C216). Both support conclusion that unconventional secretion is more affected. OpenEval notes ESCRT/GRASP observation is important negative result; peer review accepts this within demonstration of EV involvement.

Both uncertain about lipid metabolism mechanism (C217-C226). OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN, noting limited direct evidence and need for experimental validation. Peer review does not explicitly evaluate but editor notes mechanisms 'not yet fully understood,' suggesting acknowledgment of mechanistic gaps.

Divergent evaluation of Ire1 mechanism (C227-C230). OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED based on HXL1 splicing data and reasonable hypothesis with correlative evidence. Peer review does not explicitly evaluate these mechanistic speculations, neither affirming nor challenging them.

Both uncertain about tetraspanin mechanism (C231-C232). OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN, noting this is speculation from different organism without direct C. neoformans evidence. Peer review does not explicitly evaluate but groups with mechanistic speculations that are neither affirmed nor challenged.

Peer review evaluates extensive background and novelty claims (C1, C15-C56) that OpenEval does not address as a separate result. Peer reviewers accept the background context and novelty claim, describing this as an 'important study' with 'novel data.'
